speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition better, could you describe the nature of your diarrhea—is it watery, contains mucus or blood, and how long has this been going on? Also, on a scale of 1 to 10, how severe is your lower abdominal discomfort?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. To narrow down the cause, I need to know if you have experienced any unintentional weight loss, fever, or blood in your stool during these four months. Additionally, have you noticed any changes in your symptoms related to stress or specific foods?

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the infectious workup is negative and your symptoms—specifically urgency, mucus, and relief with defecation—are classic for Irritable Bowel Syndrome, I need to rule out inflammatory bowel disease. Do you have any family history of inflammatory bowel disease or celiac disease?
